units: <cite ref="Aramaic Targum to Song of Songs 1:2">Targ. Cant. I, 2</cite> <he>בג׳</he> for verbal study.—
<cite ref="Megillah 6b:4">Meg. 6ᵇ</cite> <he>לאוקומי ג׳ וכ׳</he> to preserve (in memory) what one has learned requires divine assistance.
<cite ref="Shabbat 21b:2">Sabb. 21ᵇ</cite> <he>ג׳ דינקותא</he> what has been learned in youth (which is better remembered).
<cite ref="Shabbat 30b:1">Ib. 30ᵇ</cite> <he>לא הוה פסיק פומיה מג׳</he> did not cease reciting.
<cite ref="Eruvin 68a:3">Erub. 68ᵃ</cite> <he>אנא</he> … <he>בגִרְסָאִי</he> I am busy studying; a. fr.—Pl. <he>גִּרְסַיָּיא</he>, <cite ref="C01277"><he>גִּירְ׳</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Bava Batra 22a:3">B. Bath. 22ᵃ</cite> <he>דלא ליטרדו מגִּירְסַיְיהוּ</he> Ms. M. (ed. <he>אתו ליטרדו מג׳</he>) that they may not be disturbed in their studies.

Yalk. Gen. 84 ג׳ אחרינא זה וכ׳ another version (for זה איוב, Gen. R. s. 50) is, ‘This alludes to the tribe of Levi’. [Frequently in commentaries.—Denom. גרס to read. הכי גרסינן (abbr. ה״ג) such is the proper reading.]
